multiview supervised dictionary learning in speech emotion recognition.
multiview supervised dictionary learning in the application of emotion recognition.
the development of multiview learning methods based on the HSIC-based supervised dictionary learning and their application in the problem of SER.

the proposed multivew dictionary learning approach outperforms the other approaches in terms of the correlation coefficient.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed multiverview learning approach achieves a better performance in SER compared to the baseline system of AVEC 2011, and also the single-view and multiview approaches in the literature.
by providing the complementary information of two views, the proposed approaches outperform the single views in predicting continuous dimensional affects of speech.
by learning a single dictionary and corresponding coefficients in the feature space of fused views, a better performance is achieved in SER compared to the other multiview learning methods.
The main takeaway from our work is that

by using the proposed multilabel HSIC-based dictionary learning approach, the performance of the baseline system in the AVEC 2102 dataset is improved from 0.47 to 0.54 in terms of the correlation coefficient.
the proposed multivew techniques are able to learn a more discriminative dictionary in the space of features of each view, and consequently achieve better performance in SER.
the HSIC-based SDL is a promising approach for multiview supervised learning.
